correctness.rationale: Explicit Pappus incidence and Desargues Petersen-double-cover graph definitions agree under hardcoded edge-by-edge isomorphisms with independent LCF/GP encodings. The exact monotone forcing closure is proved equivalent to sequential forcing. Two standalone programs exhaust all 63004 subsets of Pappus size at most 7 and all 263950 Desargues subsets size at most 8, reject all smaller sets, and recover respectively 6912 and 13520 minima. They enumerate all legal slides, both check Pappus 10962 edges and Desargues zero edges, and compute connected components; each computes all 6912 source-distance eccentricities (648/4968/1296 at 16/17/18). Both confirm Desargues jumping connected with 178560 edges by different transition generation. Finite certificates do not assert an infinite result.

value.rationale: The precise adjacency restriction is motivated by physically local reassignment of an initially forced sensor. Pappus and Desargues are canonical regular bipartite girth-six incidence graphs, yet one has all optimal configurations mutually accessible by local moves (sharp radius 16, diameter 18) and the other none, despite connected unrestricted swaps. The two-graph contrast demonstrates that coarse local base-graph parameters and unrestricted mobility cannot predict locality-restricted mobility. The exact finite state census and distance spectrum are natural complete invariants, not an arbitrary numerical slice; the motivation is independent of mere reproducibility.
